chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever performs an obligatory duty; for him with Allah is a supplication that will be answered.

key_terms.فَرِيضَة: Obligatory duty or act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing an obligatory act of worship in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to emphasize the spiritual efficacy of obligatory acts (fara'id) as a means to secure divine acceptance. This tradition underscores the Shia understanding that consistent fulfillment of religious duties establishes a covenantal bond with Allah, ensuring that subsequent supplications are met with favor. It serves as both a spiritual incentive for adherence to Sharia and a reminder of the reciprocal nature of worship and divine response.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-22 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
After one says his obligatory prayers, one of his needs for which he prays will be fulfilled.”
